title: Bank of America added 1,000 contractors to patch flaws found with Mythos
friendlyTitle: Bank of America hired 1,000 contractors to patch AI-found software flaws
summary: CEO Brian Moynihan said the bank put 1,000 contractors alongside about 3,000 internal staff to patch software flaws exposed by advanced models, including Anthropic's Mythos. He also said software remediation and separate anti-money-laundering compliance together added a couple of hundred million dollars of third-quarter cost.
friendlySummary: Bank of America's chief executive said the bank added 1,000 contractors to help fix software flaws found with advanced AI, including Anthropic's Mythos. He said that work, plus other compliance costs, added a large bill last quarter.
whyItMatters: Stronger AI can create a security bill before it creates savings. Moynihan still expects the bank's own AI projects to reduce expenses over time, but organisations adopting frontier models should budget for the cleanup those models can force.
friendlyWhyItMatters: Better AI can save money later, but it can also reveal expensive security work now. Companies using powerful models should plan for that cleanup cost.
